title: AP Precalculus 2.15 — Semi-log Plots
question: Semi-log plots: read a log scale, spot straight data, turn the line into a model, predict, and read a growth rate.
intro:
**Quick recap:**

\[
\begin{aligned}
y &= a\cdot b^{x} \\
\log y &= \log a+x\log b
\end{aligned}
\]

- On a semi-log plot exponential data is a **straight line**.
- Slope \(=\log b\), intercept \(=\log a\).
- Equal gaps on the log axis are equal factors.

**A calculator is allowed. Show your calculation before choosing A–D.**

questions.title: Read a log scale
questions.prompt: On the log-scale \(y\)-axis of a semi-log plot, a point sits exactly halfway between the gridlines \(10\) and \(100\). What is its \(y\)-value?
questions.solution_title: Halfway in height is halfway in log y
questions.solution:
- The height on a log scale is \(\log y\).
- \(\log10=1\) and \(\log100=2\), so halfway is \(1.5\).

\[
\begin{aligned}
\log y &= 1.5 \\
y &= 10^{1.5} \\
&\approx 31.6
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{y\approx31.6}
\]

- Not \(55\): that is halfway on an ordinary scale.
- Not \(50\) or \(15\): the gap from \(10\) to \(100\) is a factor of \(10\), so halfway is a factor of \(\sqrt{10}\approx3.16\).

questions.title: Which data is straight?
questions.prompt: Each set has \(x=0,1,2,3\). Which set of \(y\)-values lies on a **straight line** on a semi-log plot?
questions.solution_title: Look for the same ratio each step
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
21\div7 &= 3 \\
63\div21 &= 3 \\
189\div63 &= 3
\end{aligned}
\]

- Same ratio \(3\) every step: exponential, so straight on a semi-log plot.

\[
\boxed{7,\ 21,\ 63,\ 189}
\]

- Not \(2,4,6,8\): adds \(2\) each step (linear).
- Not \(1,4,9,16\): \(y=x^{2}\), the ratios \(4,\ 2.25,\ 1.78\) change.
- Not \(10,20,40,70\): \(\times2,\ \times2,\) then \(\times1.75\). One different ratio is enough to bend.

questions.title: From the line to the model
questions.prompt:
On a semi-log plot (\(\log\) base \(10\)) the data lie on the line

\[
\log y=0.3+0.6x
\]

Which model fits, to one decimal place?
questions.solution_title: Intercept is log a, slope is log b
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\log a &= 0.3 \\
a &= 10^{0.3} \\
&\approx 2.0 \\
\log b &= 0.6 \\
b &= 10^{0.6} \\
&\approx 4.0
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{y\approx2.0\cdot(4.0)^{x}}
\]

- Not \(4.0\cdot(2.0)^{x}\): intercept and slope swapped.
- Not \(0.3+0.6x\) or \(0.3\cdot0.6^{x}\): the line is for \(\log y\); undo the \(\log\) with \(10^{(\ )}\).

questions.title: Predict from two points
questions.prompt: The figure shows a semi-log plot. The data lie on a straight line through \((0,\,6)\) and \((2,\,54)\). Predict \(y\) at \(x=3\).
questions.figure_alt: Semi-log plot: a straight line through (0, 6) and (2, 54); a dashed guide at x = 3 marked y = ?
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
y &= a\cdot b^{x} \\
a &= 6 \\
54 &= 6\cdot b^{2} \\
b^{2} &= 9 \\
b &= 3 \\
y(3) &= 6\cdot3^{3} \\
&= 162
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{162}
\]

- Not \(78\): a straight line on an ordinary graph (\(6+24x\)) is the wrong model here.
- Not \(108\): one step multiplies by \(3\), not by \(2\).
- Not \(486\): \(54\cdot9\) jumps two steps; \(x=3\) is one step after \(x=2\).

questions.title: Growth rate from the slope
questions.prompt: An app's monthly downloads lie on a straight line on a semi-log plot (\(\log\) base \(10\)). The slope of the line is \(0.0792\) per month. By what percent do the downloads grow each month?
questions.solution_title: Slope is log b; b - 1 is the rate
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\log b &= 0.0792 \\
b &= 10^{0.0792} \\
&\approx 1.20
\end{aligned}
\]

- \(b=1.20\) means \(\times1.20\) each month: \(+20\%\).

\[
\boxed{\text{about }20\%}
\]

- Not \(7.92\%\) or \(0.0792\%\): the slope is \(\log b\), not the rate.
- Not \(120\%\): \(1.20\) is the factor; the growth is the part above \(1\).

takeaway: Straight on a semi-log plot means exponential: slope = log b, intercept = log a.
